questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $O$ with initial speed $30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and passes through a point which is at a horizontal distance $60\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$ and a distance $20\ \mathrm{m}$ vertically above the level of $O$. Show that there are two possible angles of projection.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Take $O$ as origin, $x$ horizontal in the direction of projection and $y$ vertically upwards (positive upwards, acceleration $-g$). The particle is projected with speed $u = 30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal and moves under gravity only. The value $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ is used (no value is printed in this question).

$$x = (u\cos\theta)\,t,\qquad y = (u\sin\theta)\,t - \tfrac12 g t^2$$

Eliminating $t$ gives the equation of the path, with $T = \tan\theta$ and $\sec^2\theta = 1 + T^2$:

$$y = x\tan\theta - \frac{g x^2}{2u^2}\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right)$$

The path passes through the point $(x, y) = (60, 20)$. With $u^2 = 900$, so $\dfrac{g x^2}{2u^2} = \dfrac{g\times 3600}{1800} = 2g$:

$$20 = 60T - 2g\left(1 + T^2\right) \;\Rightarrow\; g\,T^2 - 30\,T + (g + 10) = 0$$

With $g = 9.8$, multiplying by $5$: $\ 49T^2 - 150T + 99 = 0$.

Discriminant: $\Delta = 150^2 - 4\times 49\times 99 = 22500 - 19404 = 3096 > 0$.

The discriminant is positive, so the quadratic in $\tan\theta$ has two distinct real roots:

$$\tan\theta = \frac{150 \pm \sqrt{3096}}{98} = \frac{75 \pm 3\sqrt{86}}{49} \approx 2.098 \ \text{ or } \ 0.963$$

Both roots are positive, so both give an angle between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$: $\theta \approx 64.5^\circ$ and $\theta \approx 43.9^\circ$. **Hence there are two possible angles of projection.** $\blacksquare$

(With $g = 10$ the equation is $T^2 - 3T + 2 = 0$, with roots $T = 1$ and $T = 2$, that is $45^\circ$ and $63.4^\circ$; the conclusion is the same.)

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $O$ with initial speed $30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and passes through a point which is at a horizontal distance $60\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$ and a distance $20\ \mathrm{m}$ vertically above the level of $O$. If these angles are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, prove that $\tan(\alpha + \beta) = -3$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $\tan\alpha$ and $\tan\beta$ be the two roots of the quadratic found in (a), $g\,T^2 - 30\,T + (g + 10) = 0$. For a quadratic $AT^2 + BT + C = 0$ the sum and the product of the roots are $-B/A$ and $C/A$:

$$\tan\alpha + \tan\beta = \frac{30}{g},\qquad \tan\alpha\,\tan\beta = \frac{g + 10}{g}$$

Hence $\ 1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta = 1 - \dfrac{g + 10}{g} = -\dfrac{10}{g}$.

Using the addition formula for the tangent:

$$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta} = \frac{30/g}{-10/g} = -3.\qquad\blacksquare$$

(Numerical check with $g = 9.8$: the sum is $\dfrac{150}{49}$, the product $\dfrac{99}{49}$, and $\dfrac{150/49}{1 - 99/49} = \dfrac{150}{-50} = -3$; the result does not depend on $g$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle of mass $m\ \mathrm{kg}$ moves on the inside surface of a smooth spherical bowl of radius $2a$, describing a horizontal circle at a distance $a$ below the centre of the bowl. Prove that its speed is $\sqrt{3ag}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Let $C$ be the centre of the bowl and $P$ the particle, with $CP = 2a$. The particle moves in a horizontal circle whose plane is at a depth $a$ below $C$, so if $\varphi$ is the angle between $CP$ and the downward vertical,

$$\cos\varphi = \frac{a}{2a} = \frac12 \;\Rightarrow\; \varphi = 60^\circ,\qquad r = 2a\sin 60^\circ = \sqrt3\,a$$

where $r$ is the radius of the circle. Forces on $P$ (the bowl is smooth): the weight $mg$ downwards and the normal reaction $N$ along $PC$, that is inclined at $60^\circ$ to the vertical, directed upwards and towards the axis of the circle. The speed $v$ is constant; the acceleration is $\dfrac{v^2}{r}$ horizontally, towards the axis.

**Vertical** (no vertical acceleration): $\ N\cos 60^\circ = mg \;\Rightarrow\; N = 2mg$.

**Horizontal** (towards the axis): $\ N\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{m v^2}{r}$:

$$2mg\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2} = \frac{m v^2}{\sqrt3\,a} \;\Rightarrow\; \sqrt3\,mg = \frac{m v^2}{\sqrt3\,a} \;\Rightarrow\; v^2 = 3ag$$

**Hence the speed is $v = \sqrt{3ag}$.** $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle of mass $m\ \mathrm{kg}$ moves on the inside surface of a smooth spherical bowl of radius $2a$, describing a horizontal circle at a distance $a$ below the centre of the bowl. Find the period of revolution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The particle travels once round the circle of radius $r = \sqrt3\,a$ at the constant speed $v = \sqrt{3ag}$ (part (c)), so the period is

$$T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi\sqrt3\,a}{\sqrt{3ag}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{3a^2}{3ag}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{a}{g}}$$

**The period of revolution is $2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{a}{g}}$ seconds.**
